palette.role: Alternative permanent canopy where very long hanging racemes are the design goal.

handedness.basis: RHS: "twine clockwise", no viewpoint stated. Clockwise viewed from above per Valder (1995) and three Japanese tree guides: a left-handed helix, the opposite of W. sinensis.

attachment.supportNeeds: Long woody routes along the glulam and its sub-lattice, plus free vertical hanging clearance beneath for racemes of a metre or more, clear of cross-members, lighting and visitors.

wood.basis: RHS: wisteria flower buds start to develop in late summer of the previous year.

monthsUK.basis: RHS record ('Kyushaku'): flowers "produced in late spring", which is May by the season rule (spring = Mar-May, summer = Jun-Aug, autumn = Sep-Nov, winter = Dec-Feb; early, mid and late are the first, second and third month). June is not stated by any source read: it rests on Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online), who says W. floribunda flowers "two or three weeks later" than W. sinensis, which "flowers towards the end of May".

flowering.display: Lilac-blue to violet pendulous racemes that can reach 1 m or more.

site.aspect: Full sun or partial shade; south or west facing, sheltered; generous overhead clearance.

calendar.note: Summer: cut the whippy green shoots of the current year back to five or six leaves.
Winter: cut the same shoots back to two or three buds.

management.notes: Train and selectively thin; two-stage wisteria pruning while protecting productive laterals; inspect for attachment constriction.

hazards: Long racemes need clear height above circulation.
Mature woody mass and wind response are not validated.
